To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

2-hydroxynitrobenzaldehyde bromide reacts with cytochrome c to form a single species, which is a monomer and is modified at the tryptophan residue, and that the chemically modified protein has a pH-dependent spectral change which is typical of an alpha/beta species, is autoxidized, binds CO and CN- and has lost its electron transfer activity.

the chemical modification of cytochrome C with a fluorescent probe, 2-Hydro-xy-5-nitrbenzyl bromid, results in a protein that has lost its ability to transfer electrons, but retains the ability to bind ligands.
the chemical modification of cytochrome C with 2-hyroxy-5-nitrbenzyl bromides results in the loss of the electron transfer activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation and characterization of a chemically modified form of cytochrome.
the preparation and some properties, including electron-transfer properties, of chemically modified cytochrome C.
the effects of a single modification on the functional properties of cytochrome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reagent has reacted with a histidine residue, and the changes observed are consistent with this.
the modified cytochromes are not functionally active.
the modified protein is a functional cytochrome c analogue, but not an analogue of the native protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reagent has modified the protein so that the molecule is no longer capable of functioning as a physiological electron carrier.
2-hydroxyl-5-nitrobzyl bromide modifies the protein in such a way as to destroy the ability of the modified cyochrome c to function in electron transport.
the introduction of a nitrobenzyl moiety into cytochrome c causes marked changes in its properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of a small molecule at one or more sites of a protein may have a significant effect on the functional properties of the protein.
a single modification of a protein can result in a large number of changes in the functional properties.

the introduction of the 2-hydroxynitrobenzaldehyde group in the vicinity of the heme group of cytochrome C has profound effects on the properties of the molecule, including the loss of electron-transfer activity.
